title: Best Affordable Tools to Mass Apply to Jobs Without Overpaying in 2026
summary: Price per application for 8 mass-apply tools in 2026: LazyApply from $0.002 if used daily for a year, Tsenta $0.022 to $0.032 monthly, LoopCV $0.20.
body_markdown:
**The cheapest way to mass apply to jobs is to start on a free tier, then pay for the plan with the lowest price per submitted application at the volume you will really use.** On prices checked November 13, 2026, Tsenta costs $0.022 to $0.032 per submitted application on monthly billing after 25 free applications, LazyApply drops under 2 cents only if you use its full daily cap for the year you pay upfront, and LoopCV's free plan sends up to 10 applications or emails a month.


Updated November 13, 2026. Tsenta publishes this comparison and sells one of the tools in it. We read every price, cap and free tier off each company's own pricing or help page on November 13, 2026; we did not buy each plan or run a live application test. This guide is about cost. For speed and volume, see[the best tools to mass apply to multiple jobs fast](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-tools-mass-apply-multiple-jobs-fast) , and for how Tsenta applies at volume, see[mass apply with an AI agent](https://tsenta.com/mass-apply) .


## Cost per application: eight mass-apply tools compared


Prices as of November 13, 2026. Effective cost per application divides the plan price by its full allowance, so it is the lowest you can pay, reached only if you use every application. Prices are in US dollars and can differ by country, billing period and app store.

How we worked out Tsenta's figures: plan price divided by applications per cycle. On monthly billing that is $19 / 600 = $0.032 (Starter), $39 / 1,500 = $0.026 (Pro) and $99 / 4,500 = $0.022 (Power). Quarterly billing ($49, $79, $239 for three cycles) brings it to $0.027, $0.018 and $0.018. Annual billing ($159, $299, $799 for twelve cycles) brings it to $0.022, $0.017 and $0.015. These are the global USD prices; the[pricing page](https://tsenta.com/pricing) and checkout show your market's price.


How we worked out the others: Simplify+ monthly assumes a 30-day month holds 30 / 7, about 4.3 weekly resets, so about 86 credits for $39.99. LazyApply assumes 365 days of use at the full daily cap. JobCopilot divides the "starts from" daily rate by the daily match cap. AIApply divides each Auto Apply plan price by its applications, before tailoring add-ons. LoopCV prices are the US dollar prices its pricing page showed a US visitor; the same page's FAQ says paid plans start from €9.99 a month.


**Where others win on cost.** If you use its daily cap all year and its job boards cover your search, LazyApply's Premium and Ultimate plans cost less per application than any Tsenta plan, and Basic costs less than Tsenta's monthly plans. LoopCV's free plan, up to 10 applications or emails a month, has no time limit. JobCopilot's Elite starting rate, about 2 cents per match, is close to Tsenta Power. Simplify's free Copilot costs nothing if you are willing to submit each form yourself. AIApply's unused Auto Apply credits carry into the next cycle while you stay subscribed, while Tsenta's unused plan applications do not roll over.


## What counts as an application: true submission vs autofill


The cheapest price per application means little if the tools count different things.


- **Submitted applications.** Tsenta counts a form actually submitted to an employer. Simplify+ Autopilot spends a credit only on a successful submission. AIApply uses one Auto Apply credit only when an application is submitted successfully.
- **Applications or emails.** LoopCV's allowance counts applications and emails together.
- **Job matches.** JobCopilot caps job matches a day. A match is a role found for you, not proof that an application went out.
- **Autofill you submit.** Simplify's free Copilot and Jobright's 1-click autofill fill the form, and you press submit. That saves typing, but you still do every application.


## The tools, ranked by price per application, upfront cost and what's included


We ranked by published price per submitted application, how much you must pay upfront, and what each application includes. On price per application alone, LazyApply's Premium and Ultimate plans come first. Tsenta sells one of these tools, so check the sources in the table.


### 1. Tsenta: $0.022 to $0.032 per submitted application, tailoring included


Tsenta is an AI job application agent. It finds roles for your match feed, optimizes your résumé for each one, drafts a cover letter when the form takes one, submits on the employer's own system across[30+ supported employer systems](https://tsenta.com/ai-disclosure) including Workday, and adds the result to your tracker. Applications run in Tsenta's cloud.


- **Price:** the first 25 applications are free, once, with no card. Then Starter is $19 a month for 600 applications, Pro $39 for 1,500 and Power $99 for 4,500, per 30-day cycle. Annual Power brings the cost to $0.015 an application.
- **What counts:** only a successful submission. Failed attempts, skipped matches and drafts you never approved go back to your allowance automatically.
- **Included on every plan:** résumé optimization for each role, a cover letter when the form takes one, the tracker and recruiter reply monitoring, on the web, the[iPhone app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tsenta/id6760728258) , the[Android app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tsenta.tsenta) , the Chrome extension, iMessage, WhatsApp and the[MCP server](https://tsenta.com/mcp) .
- **What Power adds:** Auto Apply, which picks and submits new matches without asking you to approve each role. On Starter and Pro you choose each role.


Where it costs more: if you only need 100 applications a month, Starter still costs $19, or $0.19 each. Unused applications do not roll over. If you run out before your cycle resets, any paid plan can add pay-per-application funds on the web at 10 cents an application, and those credits do not expire. Upgrading is cheaper if you run out often. See[plans and what counts as one application](https://help.tsenta.com/plans-and-pricing) .


### 2. LazyApply: cheapest on paper, if you use the daily cap all year


LazyApply sells annual plans only: Basic at $99 a year for 15 applications a day, Premium at $149 for 150 and Ultimate at $999 for 1,500. It applies on platforms it names, such as Greenhouse, Dice, Indeed and ZipRecruiter.


Where it wins: used every day for a year, Basic costs about $0.018 an application, Premium about $0.003 and Ultimate about $0.002. Premium and Ultimate are the lowest figures in this guide. Where it costs more: you pay the year upfront, so a one-month search on Basic works out to about $0.22 an application. Its plan list names résumé profiles, analytics and support, not résumé tailoring for each role. It lists no free plan. It advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee, but its refund policy covers only a first subscription, only if you applied to fewer than 100 jobs, and only when the product demonstrably fails to work as advertised. See[Tsenta vs LazyApply](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-lazyapply) .


### 3. LoopCV: a free plan with no time limit


LoopCV runs saved job searches, which it calls loops, across job boards and applies for you. Basic Looper is free, needs no card and allows up to 10 applications or emails a month. For a US visitor, its pricing page showed Standard Looper at $19.99 a month for up to 100 applications or emails, Premium Looper at $59.99 for up to 300, and Done For You at $89.99 with Premium's limits plus a weekly advisory call.


Where it wins: the free plan has no time limit, and LoopCV refunds within 7 days of purchase if you used no more than 10% of your quota. Where it costs more: Standard is about $0.20 per application or email, roughly six times Tsenta Starter's $0.032, and emails count against the same allowance. See[Tsenta vs LoopCV](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-loopcv) .


### 4. JobCopilot: a low daily rate, counted in job matches


JobCopilot prices by the day: Premium from $0.93 with up to 20 job matches daily, and Elite from $1.05 with up to 50. Elite adds résumé tailoring for every application and three copilots instead of one. Weekly, monthly and quarterly plans are available, but the pricing page shows only the daily starting rates.


Where it wins: at the starting rate, Elite is about 2 cents per match if every match is used. Where to be careful: a job match is not a submitted application, the billed total appears only at checkout, and the pricing page lists no free plan. See[Tsenta vs JobCopilot](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobcopilot) .


### 5. Simplify: free autofill, paid Autopilot at about 47 cents


Simplify's Copilot autofill, résumé builder and job tracker are free, and you submit each form yourself. Autopilot, part of Simplify+, fills and submits without a review step and uses 20 credits a week, one per successful submission. Simplify+ costs $19.99 a week, $39.99 a month or $89.99 every 3 months on the web.


Where it wins: Copilot is free if you want to apply by hand faster, and failed or cancelled Autopilot runs do not use a credit. Where it costs more: Autopilot works out to about $0.47 an application on monthly billing and $1.00 on weekly billing, and 20 a week limits volume. Unused credits do not roll over. See[Tsenta vs Simplify](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-simplify) .


### 6. AIApply: Auto Apply from about 25 cents, tailoring extra


AIApply sells Auto Apply on its own: $49 a month for 100 applications, $99 a month for 250 or $199 a quarter for 750, and its help center lists upgrades up to $499 for 2,000. A credit is used only when an application is submitted, so failed attempts and skipped listings cost nothing. A tailored résumé and a tailored cover letter for Auto Apply are add-ons at $12 a month each. Its Premium toolkit, $29 a month or $144 a year, covers writing tools such as its résumé builder and cover letter generator and is a separate subscription.


Where it wins: unused Auto Apply credits carry into the next cycle while you stay subscribed, which Tsenta's plan allowance does not. Where it costs more: about $0.40 to $0.49 an application on monthly billing, $0.27 on the quarterly plan and $0.25 on the largest upgrade, before tailoring. Credits are lost if you cancel and let the subscription lapse, and AIApply says its fees are generally non-refundable. See[Tsenta vs AIApply](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-aiapply) .


### 7. Jobright: a free start, no public job-seeker price


Jobright offers a free start and markets 1-click autofill across ATS platforms, plus an AI agent page with an Auto-Apply option. It publishes no job-seeker prices: jobright.ai/pricing returns "Page not found", and the Pricing link in its menu leads to employer recruiting plans.


Where it wins: a free way to get matched jobs and autofill. Where to be careful: with no public price or allowance, you cannot compare its cost per application until you are in the product. See[Tsenta vs Jobright](https://tsenta.com/blog/tsenta-vs-jobright) .


### 8. Sonara: no price we could confirm


We could not confirm Sonara's price, cap or free tier on November 13, 2026. Its old pricing page at m.sonara.ai/pricing returns "Page not found", and sonara.ai did not load for us. If you consider it, check the plan, the application cap and the renewal terms at checkout before you pay.


## Hidden costs: credits, per-application fees and refunds


A low headline price can still cost more than you expect. Check these before you pay.


- **Credits that expire.** Simplify+ gives 20 credits a week and unused ones do not roll over. Tsenta's allowance resets each 30-day cycle and does not roll over either, though pay-per-application funds you add do not expire. AIApply's Auto Apply page says its credits never expire, but[its help center](https://support.aiapply.co/en/articles/15070980-what-happens-to-credits-when-a-subscription-ends-or-is-downgraded) says unused credits carry over only while your subscription is active and are lost if you cancel and let it lapse.
- **Per-application fees on top of a plan.** AIApply sells Auto Apply apart from its $29 toolkit, and a tailored résumé and a tailored cover letter for Auto Apply cost $12 a month each on top. Any paid Tsenta plan can add pay-per-application funds on the web at 10 cents an application after the allowance runs out.
- **Upfront billing.** LazyApply bills a full year, $99 to $999, before your first application. Tsenta, Simplify+, LoopCV, JobCopilot and AIApply Auto Apply offer shorter billing periods.
- **Counts that are not submissions.** JobCopilot caps matches and LoopCV counts emails, so their per-unit price is not a price per submitted application.
- **Refunds.** LazyApply advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee, but[its refund policy](https://lazyapply.com/refundpolicy) covers only a first subscription, only if you applied to fewer than 100 jobs, and only when the product demonstrably fails to work as advertised. LoopCV refunds within 7 days if you used no more than 10% of your quota.[AIApply's refund policy](https://support.aiapply.co/en/articles/15069772-what-is-aiapply-s-refund-policy) says its fees are generally non-refundable. It considers a refund for a reproducible technical issue or for an accidental purchase reported within 30 minutes, and Auto Apply is not refundable once applications have been submitted. Tsenta refunds failed, skipped and unapproved applications to your allowance automatically; for money back on a web plan, emailfounders@tsenta.com , and App Store or Google Play plans go through Apple or Google. See[billing, refunds and cancelling](https://help.tsenta.com/billing-refunds-and-cancelling) .


## Cost vs quality


A cheap application helps only if it reaches a role you fit with materials that match it. Before you compare prices, compare what one application includes:


- **Résumé tailoring.** Included on every Tsenta plan, on JobCopilot Elite only, inside each Simplify+ Autopilot credit, and as a separate subscription for AIApply Auto Apply.
- **Review.** Tsenta's résumé review lets you approve each change before it goes out, and compatible employer forms can pause for review before submit. Simplify's Autopilot submits without a review step, and JobCopilot lets you save applications for review.
- **Where it applies.** Tsenta submits on the employer's own site, across 30+ supported employer systems. LazyApply and LoopCV name job boards and platforms. Check that your target employers are covered before you count on the volume.


## How to mass apply without overpaying


1. **Start free.** Use Tsenta's 25 free applications, LoopCV's free plan or Simplify's free Copilot to see which workflow fits.
2. **Estimate your volume.** About 20 applications a day is 600 per 30 days, Tsenta Starter's allowance. About 50 a day is 1,500, Pro's.
3. **Match billing to your search.** For a one- or two-month search, monthly billing usually beats an annual plan you will not use up.
4. **Price the extras.** Add tailoring, extra credits and any second subscription before you compare.
5. **Read the refund terms.** Know the window and the conditions before you pay.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the cheapest way to mass apply to jobs?


Start on a free tier, then pay for the plan with the lowest price per submitted application at the volume you will really use. Tsenta gives you 25 free applications with no card, then costs $0.022 to $0.032 per submitted application on monthly billing: $19 for 600, $39 for 1,500 or $99 for 4,500 per 30-day cycle. LazyApply can be cheaper on paper, from under 2 cents an application down to a fraction of a cent, but only if you use its full daily cap for the whole year it bills upfront. LoopCV's free plan sends up to 10 applications or emails a month at no cost. Prices checked November 13, 2026.


### How much do auto apply tools cost per application?


From about $0.002 to about $1 per application in 2026, depending on the tool, the billing period and what it counts. On monthly billing, Tsenta costs $0.022 to $0.032 per submitted application, LoopCV about $0.20 per application or email, AIApply Auto Apply about $0.40 to $0.49, and Simplify+ Autopilot about $0.47 per submission, or $1.00 on weekly billing. LazyApply works out to $0.002 to $0.018 if you use every daily application for a year. Jobright publishes no job-seeker price, and we could not confirm Sonara's. Each figure divides the price by the full allowance, so it is the lowest you can pay.


### How many auto applies does Simplify+ include per week, and what does it cost?


Simplify+ includes 20 Autopilot credits a week, and each successful submission uses one. It costs $19.99 a week, $39.99 a month or $89.99 every 3 months on the web, and Simplify says App Store pricing can differ. Unused credits do not roll over, and failed or cancelled runs do not use a credit. On monthly billing that is about $0.47 per Autopilot application if you use every credit. Simplify's Copilot autofill is free, but you submit each form yourself.


### How much does JobCopilot cost, and how many applications a day?


JobCopilot's pricing page lists Premium from $0.93 a day with up to 20 job matches daily and Elite from $1.05 a day with up to 50. It says weekly, monthly and quarterly plans are available but does not show their totals, so check the price at checkout. Its homepage says you can send up to 50 personalized applications a day. At the starting daily rate, that is about 5 cents (Premium) or 2 cents (Elite) per match if you use every match. A match is not the same as a submitted application.


### How much does LoopCV cost for auto apply?


LoopCV has a free plan with up to 10 applications or emails a month, and paid plans from $19.99 a month in US dollars. Its pricing page showed a US visitor Standard Looper at $19.99 a month for up to 100 applications or emails, Premium Looper at $59.99 for up to 300, and Done For You at $89.99, with lower 3-month prices. That is about $0.20 per application or email on Standard and Premium. The same page's FAQ says paid plans start from €9.99 a month, so the price can differ by region.


### How much does LazyApply cost?


LazyApply sells three annual plans: Basic at $99 a year for 15 applications a day, Premium at $149 for 150 a day, and Ultimate at $999 for 1,500 a day. It lists no free plan. It advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee, but its refund policy covers only a first subscription, only if you applied to fewer than 100 jobs, and only when the product demonstrably fails to work as advertised. Used every day for a year, Basic works out to under 2 cents an application. If your search lasts one month, the same $99 covers about 450 applications, or 22 cents each.


### What hidden costs should I check before paying for an auto-apply tool?


Check four things: credits that expire, per-application fees on top of the plan, upfront billing and the refund terms. Simplify+ credits reset weekly and do not roll over, and Tsenta's allowance resets each 30-day cycle without rolling over. AIApply's unused Auto Apply credits carry over only while you stay subscribed and are lost if you cancel and let the subscription lapse. AIApply also sells Auto Apply separately from its $29 a month toolkit, and a tailored résumé and a tailored cover letter for Auto Apply cost $12 a month each. LazyApply bills a full year upfront. On any paid Tsenta plan, you can add pay-per-application funds on the web when your allowance runs out, at 10 cents an application. Those credits do not expire, but they cost more than upgrading if you run out often.


### Can I get a refund from an auto-apply tool?


Sometimes, and the terms differ by tool. LazyApply advertises a 30-day money-back guarantee, but its refund policy covers only a first subscription, only if you applied to fewer than 100 jobs, and only when the product demonstrably fails to work as advertised. LoopCV refunds within 7 days of purchase if you used no more than 10% of your plan's application quota. AIApply says its fees are generally non-refundable. It considers a refund for a reproducible technical issue or for an accidental purchase reported within 30 minutes, and Auto Apply is not refundable once applications have been submitted. Tsenta returns failed applications, skipped matches and drafts you never approved to your allowance automatically. For money back on a Tsenta web plan you emailfounders@tsenta.com , and App Store or Google Play plans are refunded by Apple or Google.


### Is the cheapest auto-apply tool worth it, or does quality suffer?


A low price per application is worth it only when each application goes to a role you fit, with materials that match it. Compare what one application includes, not just how many you get. Tsenta includes résumé optimization for each role, a cover letter when the form takes one, and tracking on every plan, including the free 25. JobCopilot lists résumé tailoring for every application on Elite only, and AIApply sells tailoring for Auto Apply as a separate subscription. If quality matters more than speed, keep résumé review on and approve each change before it goes out.


### What are the best tools to mass apply to jobs?


Tsenta, LazyApply, LoopCV, JobCopilot, Simplify+ and AIApply all automate applications, and they differ most in price per application and in where they apply. On cost, Tsenta charges $0.022 to $0.032 per submitted application with résumé tailoring on every plan, and LazyApply is cheaper on paper if your search fits the job boards it names. For a comparison by speed and volume rather than price, see our guide to the[best tools to mass apply to multiple jobs fast](https://tsenta.com/blog/best-tools-mass-apply-multiple-jobs-fast) .
